Definition: from G3358; to measure (i.e. ascertain in size by a fixed standard); by implication, to admeasure (i.e. allot by rule):--figuratively, to estimate:--measure, mete.
BiblicalUsage: Jesus says with what measure you mete it shall be measured to you again, and to give with good measure, pressed down and shaken together. John shows the same word at the temple, where the angel tells him to measure the temple of God and the altar. Measuring is both a warning and a calling.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the measure we use is the measure we will be judged by: give generously and it comes back pressed down and running over, judge harshly and the same measure finds us. The measure is in our hands every day, and God will use the one we choose.
